chapter: Recent years and early piano influences
title: Pianist influences, Walter Bishop and Clarence Williams
summary: He names NYU, Walter Bishop and Richard McClanahan as teachers and friends, and Clarence Williams as a publisher.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: What I think we've got to get back on, we've never really talked on... The only pianist you talked about much was Erroll Garner. But I think we should talk a little bit, as you did before, about the pianists that influenced you from, you know, all the way back.
Yeah. Right up through my tenure at NYU and Big Lizzy(?), Walter Bishop, Richard McClanahan(?), that I studied with...
You mentioned Walter Bishop several times. What is your...
We've been good friends for (?) years.
But he's a writer, too, isn't he.
But does he work as a pianist or what?
Well, he works as a pianist. He does it for veterans, you know. But he had his own publishing house. He did a lot of things for... What was that... The old-time Blues publisher. What was the name?
Clarence Williams. He wrote numbers for Louis Jordan. He has quite a history. I'm supposed to go by and see him tomorrow...
